user_query: I need an object detection model to locate people, dogs, and cats in indoor and outdoor photographs. The objects may appear at different scales, under varied lighting, and may be partially occluded by furniture or other people. The model will run locally on a MacBook Air with an Apple M4 chip and 16 GB of unified memory, using Metal acceleration where supported. It should aim for a mAP@0.5:0.95 of approximately 0.40 or higher and recall of at least 0.75 for each class. Processing an image within roughly 500 milliseconds would be desirable.

available_hardware.details: MacBook Air with Apple M4 chip, Metal acceleration; unified memory 16 GB

model.description: Efficient single-stage detector optimized for on-device inference on Apple Silicon with Metal. Balances mAP@0.5:0.95 around 0.40+ and recall >= 0.75 for person, dog, and cat in indoor and outdoor scenes with varied scales and occlusions. Supports multi-scale features and is amenable to on-device quantization and CoreML/Metal deployment.

model_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: Rationale for model selection and training setup. The on-device constraint (MacBook Air with M4, Metal acceleration, 16 GB unified memory) favors a lightweight yet accurate detector. Yolov8 provides strong accuracy with good inference efficiency and has established pathways for on-device deployment (e.g., CoreML/Metal) when configured appropriately. The chosen configuration uses ciou for bounding box regression to improve localization under occlusion and scale variation, and focal loss for robust classification in potentially imbalanced data across the three target classes (person, dog, cat). AdamW is selected for stable convergence and good generalization on diverse indoor/outdoor scenes. A training plan of about 60 epochs with early stopping (patience 5) is proposed to balance convergence with overfitting risk given the large, heterogeneous data available (OpenImages, COCO, LVIS, VOC). Multi-scale training and mosaic-like augmentations are recommended to improve robustness to object size, lighting changes, and partial occlusion, which map well to the provided data sources and target metrics. The target performance (mAP@0.5:0.95 >= ~0.40 and recall >= 0.75 per class) aligns with the variety and coverage of the available data for person, dog, and cat. Latency target of 500 ms per image is addressed by the on-device Metal-accelerated path and by allowing input resolution and model scale to be tuned; real latency should be validated on target hardware. Potential fallbacks if latency becomes binding include switching to a lighter variant of the same family or reducing input resolution; alternative lightweight options (e.g., ssd300_coco) can be considered if the on-device constraints prove too strict. Measured latency and CPU feasibility are not provided in this patch and should be established via benchmarking on the actual device.
